extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry and specialists/readers of inter-universal Teichmüller theory (IUT)
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the logical-structural assertions, constraints, and explanatory criteria Mochizuki uses to justify gluing constructions, indeterminacies, and the role of log-links / ring structures in inter-universal Teichmüller theory. Focused on what relationships/identifications are permitted or prohibited when forming Θ-links, gluings, and associated auxiliary structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: NeuRng
rubrics_metrics.description: these indeterminacies (Ind1), (Ind2) may be eliminated, without affecting the essential logical structure of inter-universal Teichmüller theory, by taking the multiplicative monoids and abstract topological groups that appear in the F×μ-prime-strips ... to be equipped with rigidifications by regarding them as arising from some fixed 'neutral' ring structure (cid:6)Ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mochizuki asserts that one can remove the milder local indeterminacies (Ind1),(Ind2) by rigidifying the appearing multiplicative monoids and topological groups via a fixed neutral ring; this is presented as a legitimate move that does not alter the essential logical structure of IUT. It is used as a premise in later discussion of more severe indeterminacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: NeuORInd (dilemma from rigidification)
rubrics_metrics.description: working with such a fixed 'neutral' ring structure (cid:6)Ring as in (NeuRng) means either that (NeuORInd1) there is no relationship between '*' and (cid:6)Ring, or that (NeuORInd2) the relationship between '*' and (cid:6)Ring is always necessarily subject to an indeterminacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as an unavoidable dichotomy if one imposes the neutral-ring rigidification in the presence of the global assignments at stake. Mochizuki emphasizes this as a much more drastic indeterminacy than (Ind1),(Ind2) and as causing fundamental obstacles to carrying out IUT arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: PltRel
rubrics_metrics.description: "*" maps either to (cid:6)Θ-plt or — i.e., "∨"! — to (cid:6)q-plt, but not both!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rule one must adopt throughout arguments: the pilot '*' can be assigned to one or the other pilot structure (Θ-plt or q-plt) but not simultaneously to both; this enforces an exclusive OR-type relation when relating underlying labels to auxiliary pilot structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: RngRel
rubrics_metrics.description: the ring structure (cid:6)Ring is identified either with the ring structure ‡Ring or — i.e., "∨"! — with the ring structure †Ring, but not both!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel to PltRel, when regarding a 'neutral' ring structure one must identify it with one of the two ring structures on the sides of the Θ-link but cannot identify it with both simultaneously; Mochizuki uses this to argue that imposing such identifications makes IUT arguments impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of log-links and dual ring structures
rubrics_metrics.description: inter-universal Teichmüller theory requires, in an essential way, the use of the log-links, hence, in particular, [in order to define the power series of the various p-adic logarithm functions that constitute these log-links!] the ring structures †Ring, ‡Ring on both sides — i.e., "∧"! — of the Θ-link
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mochizuki asserts that the log-links and the presence of distinct ring structures on both sides of the Θ-link are indispensable to IUT: without both †Ring and ‡Ring (and their 'AND' coexistence) one cannot implement the arguments that rely on p-adic logarithm power series and the resulting constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ΘGl (allowable gluing while preserving AND)
rubrics_metrics.description: one may treat both sides of the Θ-link gluing ... as belonging to a single ring theory without disturbing [cf. the crucial AND relator "∧" property discussed in §3.4!] the gluing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a central mathematical content of the multiradial representation and holomorphic-hull construction: despite gluing two sides, one can regard them within a single ring-theoretic container while preserving the logical AND relation that is essential to IUT's Θ-pilot formalism. Mochizuki gives alternative conceptualizations (NonInf, Cohab) to understand this phenomenon.

rubrics_metrics.name: NonInf (non-interference viewpoint)
rubrics_metrics.description: One may think of (ΘGl) as a statement concerning the mutually non-interference or simultaneous executability of the Kummer theories surrounding the q-pilot and Θ-pilot relative to the gluing ... i.e., when the Kummer theory surrounding the q-pilot is held fixed, and one allows the Kummer theory surrounding the Θ-pilot to be subject to various indeterminacies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative reading of ΘGl emphasizing that one Kummer-theory can be held fixed while the other varies through indeterminacies without spoiling the gluing; useful as conceptual guidance for interpreting the multiradial representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohab (cohabitation viewpoint)
rubrics_metrics.description: One may think of (ΘGl) as a statement concerning the 'cohabitation', or 'coexistence', of the q-pilot and Θ-pilot — relative to the gluing ... — within the common container obtained by applying the multiradial representation of the Θ-pilot, forming the holomorphic hull ..., and finally taking log-volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative reading of ΘGl emphasizing a single common analytic/container construction (holomorphic hull + log-volumes) in which both pilots coexist; Mochizuki uses this to explain how computations relating q-parameters and powers can be made coherent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of explanation CnfInd1+2
rubrics_metrics.description: the situation summarized in (ΘGl) may be explained as a consequence of a 'confusion' between q-parameters and large positive powers of these q-parameters that results from the indeterminacies (Ind1), (Ind2). (This is labeled a frequently voiced misunderstanding.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mochizuki denies this common criticism: he claims that for q-parameters of sufficiently small valuation (large positive order) such a confusion cannot occur as a consequence of (Ind1),(Ind2), because those indeterminacies amount to automorphisms of underlying topological modules (log-shells) and hence preserve orders up to bounded discrepancies. See Example 3.5.1 for the boundedness argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: CnfInd3 (role of Ind3 in 'confusion')
rubrics_metrics.description: the indeterminacy (Ind3), which constrains one to restrict one's attention to upper bounds [i.e., but not lower bounds!] on the log-volume ... is sufficient to account for the possibility of a 'confusion' of the sort summarized in (ΘGl) [i.e., between q-parameters and large positive powers of these q-parameters].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mochizuki emphasizes that Ind3, defined to identify ideals generated by arbitrary positive powers of q-parameters, is the mechanism that can produce the apparent identification between q and powers; Ind1/2 alone do not produce that effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boundedness of log-shell automorphism indeterminacies (Example 3.5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: automorphisms of the Zp-module Ik only give rise to bounded discrepancies in the orders of nonzero elements of Ok: there exists a positive integer t (depending only on k) such that for any automorphism φ : Ik → Ik and any nonzero q ∈ Ok, the absolute value of the difference between the orders of q and φ(q) is ≤ t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mochizuki gives explicit module-level constructions (U(M,n), U(Ok,n) and indices s,t) showing automorphisms permute certain graded pieces with bounded shifts. Use: to rule out 'unbounded confusion' from Ind1/2 for sufficiently small valuation q-parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluings of distinct auxiliary structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinct auxiliary structures on some common [i.e., '∧'!] underlying structure may be thought of as gluings of the distinct auxiliary structures along the common underlying structure; in general they are not necessarily mapped to one another by some automorphism of the common underlying structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mochizuki lists concrete examples (group-structure: Z/2×Z/2 vs Z/4; scheme structures of non-isomorphic curves with same topological space; distinct holomorphic structures on homeomorphic surfaces; non-isomorphic mixed-characteristic local fields; non-isomorphic liftings to Zp) to illustrate that gluing different auxiliary structures along a shared underlying structure can produce genuinely distinct objects not related by automorphisms of the underlying set/space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of coric/common structures
rubrics_metrics.description: the substantive significance of formulating the definitions of objects or constructions in terms of structures that are coric for the 'gluing/link' under consideration, that is to say, in terms of structures that are commonly shared in an invariant fashion by, hence satisfy a logical AND '∧' relation relative to, the two objects that are related to one another by the link under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mochizuki illustrates with genus: defining genus via holomorphic differentials depends on holomorphic structure (not coric), whereas defining genus via topological homology is coric; one should prefer coric structures when comparing objects glued via Θ-links to obtain invariants that are preserved under the AND relation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogy with tilts of perfectoid fields (UGΘ vs TltPh)
rubrics_metrics.description: the unit group portions of the F×μ-prime-strips that appear in the Θ-link ... bear a certain resemblance to certain phenomena that occur in the theory of tilts of perfectoid fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mochizuki develops a multi-point comparison: constructs natural isomorphisms between unit groups and exact sequences involving Qp(1), describes examples (TltEx1,TltEx2), and then pinpoints essential differences (TltDf1,TltDf2, TltDf3,TltDf4) showing why the tilt analogy is suggestive but insufficient to reproduce IUT structures; these differences are presented as evaluative criteria for whether an analogy preserves the required structures (p-adic logarithm, cyclotomic character, notion of globality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruction algorithm (RcnCh)
rubrics_metrics.description: a functorial group-theoretic algorithm in the topological group GK∞ for reconstructing the set of totally ramified characters with open image χ : GK∞ → Z×p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mochizuki notes that via local class field theory and the chosen deeply ramified tower one gets inverse/direct limit identifications enabling a functorial reconstruction of totally ramified characters from GK∞; this is used as an example of group-theoretic recoverability relevant to anabelian-type reasoning in the perfectoid/contextual set-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Destination character/cohomology obstruction (DstCh / DstHT)
rubrics_metrics.description: any isomorphism O×μ_C†k ∼→ O×μ_C‡k arising from the tilt-type diagrams fails to induce an isomorphism of the respective exact sequences 1→Qp(1)→O×(·)→O×μ→1; in particular, the induced totally ramified character ψ satisfies H0(G†k, C†k(ψ−1))≠0; equivalently the perfectoid fields †k, ‡k do not share a 'common p-adic Hodge theory'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a criterion to show that tilts / unit-group isomorphisms do not preserve key p-adic Hodge-theoretic data (cyclotomic character and vanishing of certain cohomologies), hence obstructing application of conventional p-adic Hodge techniques to such isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCTlt/RCRS/RCΘ analogies and compatibility criterion (RCΘ1, RCΘ2, RCΘ3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whereas domain and codomain copies may be isomorphic as raw objects ignoring compatibility, they do not admit isomorphisms that are compatible with the transition/homeomorphism/Θ-link; in particular for the Θ-link the (Θ±ellNF-)Hodge theaters are isomorphic if one ignores compatibility but do not admit compatible isomorphisms, and neither the pairs (Gk,Ck) nor (G†k, C†k) etc. are isomorphic regardless of imposing compatibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mochizuki formulates precise analogies with tilts and Teichmüller deformations to stress that compatibility with the link (transition morphism, homeomorphism, or Θ-link) is a rigid constraint: isomorphism ignoring compatibility is not sufficient for the constructions needed in IUT. He also notes (RCΘ2lg) that the RCΘ2 property is not used in the proofs of main results — i.e., even if one is uncertain about it, proofs are not affected, only possibly overkill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural differences making tilt-analogues useless (StrDf, TltDf3, TltDf4)
rubrics_metrics.description: various structural differences (positive characteristic of tilts, absence of p-adic logarithm analogues, lack of pro-p cyclotomic rigidity, different notions of globality, cohomological dimension differences) imply the tilt-analogue pairs are useless for constructing a theory structurally analogous to IUT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mochizuki enumerates TltDf1..TltDf4 and other aspects to conclude that while formal resemblances exist, key structural features (p-adic logarithm, cyclotomic/pro-p structure, notion of globality) are absent in the tilt setting, so one cannot transfer IUT constructions there. Use this as a checklist to decide when an analogy preserves essential ingredients.
